## Space for time 2023 - ChemoSpecR for DRIFTS subtraction spectra

This space for time substitution experiment was conducted in four experimental almond orchards that have whole orchard recycling (WOR) and control treatments. These 4 fields were each sampled in 4 replicate blocks per treatment in Summer 2023 at the University of California Kearney Agricultural Research and Extension Center (UC KARE) located in Fresno County, CA. The soils were first seived to <2 mm and then separated into POM and MAOM fractions. All POM and MAOM samples were air-dried, diluted to 10% (w/w) with pre-ground potassium bromide (KBr), and then analyzed by DRIFTS spectroscopy. Spectral subtractions were performed in OMNIC, to remove the absorbance of inorganic covalent bonds such as Si-O (which compose the mineral contribution of soil).

Space for Time Substitution Design (Fields + Years):
Field K32 (est. 2008) 15 yrs  |   33 tons wood chips/acre   | Blocks 2,3,4,6
Field K74 (est. 2017)  6 yrs  |   85 tons wood chips/acre   | Blocks 11,12,13,14
Field K92 (est. 2019)  4 yrs  |   61 tons wood chips/acre   | Blocks 1,2,3,5
Field K95 (est. 2020)  3 yrs  |   60 tons wood chips/acre   | Blocks 1,2,3,4

POM and MAOM Sample (#) shorthand key:
   [K92]         [K31]        [K74]          [K95]
1. B1 - CN    9.  B2 - CN   17. B11 - CN    25. B1 - CN
2. B2 - CN    10. B3 - CN   18. B12 - CN    26. B2 - CN
3. B3 - CN    11. B4 - CN   19. B13 - CN    27. B3 - CN
4. B5 - CN    12. B6 - CN   20. B14 - CN    28. B4 - CN
5. B1 - WC    13. B2 - WC   21. B11 - WC    29. B1 - WC
6. B2 - WC    14. B3 - WC   22. B12 - WC    30. B2 - WC
7. B3 - WC    15. B4 - WC   23. B13 - WC    31. B3 - WC
8. B5 - WC    16. B6 - WC   24. B14 - WC    32. B4 - WC 
Note: CN = Control, WC = Wood Chip treatments

# Load Libraries
```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(ChemoSpec) # This creates matrix objects from spectra csv files
library(baseline) # This performs baseline correction
library(viridis) # Used in selection of peaks
library(RColorBrewer)
library(stringr)
library(R.utils)
library(ggplot2) 
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(amap)
```
The R package (ChemoSpec) was discovered at: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ChemoSpec/vignettes/ChemoSpec.pdf
ChemoSpec was designed to take the raw (.csv) spectral data, inspect + remove bad samples, correct the baseline, remove noise, normalize the data, and then perform analysis by PCA.


## The chunk below is commented out because it collates the individual sample spectra files into an rds object.
The collated rds spectra object is provided, and can be read in using the proceeding chunk


# Get the data into ChemoSpec
One is the function files2SpectraObject, which assumes that your raw data exist as separate files in a single directory, each file containing a frequency column and an intensity column. A header row may or may not be present, and the data can be separated by any separation mark you like (typically comma, tab, semi-colon or space).
files2SpectraObject acts on all files in the current working directory with the specified fileExt so there should be no extra files of that type hanging around

The second function is matrix2SpectraObject, which assumes you have a single file containing a matrix of the data. This matrix should have frequencies in the first column, and individual sample intensities in the remaining columns. There must be a header row in the file, and it must contain the sample names (except the first entry, which marks the frequencies, is ignored).

# Plotting the Spectra
reviewAllSpectra takes the pain out of inspecting quite a few spectra (previously this was called loopThruSpectra). In base graphics mode, it shows you one spectrum at a time, and waits for a return to be typed in the console before proceeding. In ggplot2 graphics mode, all the spectra are shown at once in a web page.

plotSpectra is intended for general use and publication-quality graphics. You will generally have to play with the arguments a bit if plotting more than one spectrum.

plotSpectraJS is the interactive version of plotSpectra. It shows your data in a web page with the ability to offset the spectra and zoom as desired. For really large data sets it may be slow; see the help page for ways to avoid that.

Suppose that you wanted to focus just on the carbonyl region of these spectra; you can add the argument coord_cartesian(xlim = ...).
```{r}
# Load the SFT_POM_MAOM subtraction spectra object
SFT_POM_MAOM <- readRDS("SFT_POM_MAOM_sub_KM.rds")
# Make title and plot a couple samples
mytitle <- expression(bold(WOR~POM~and~MAOM)~bold(Oxidized~and~Untreated~IR~Spectra))
p <- plotSpectra(SFT_POM_MAOM, which = c(1, 2), yrange = c(-0.5, 0.5), # Just showing one sample
offset = 0, lab.pos = 2200) # Offset is set to zero, because the spectra will along off the y-axis
p <- p + ggtitle(mytitle)
p # when using ggplot2, you have to "call" the object containing the plot

# We can also focus on a specific region using xlim
p <- p + ggtitle(mytitle) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1200, 3700)) # carbonyl focus would be 1650, 1800
p
```

# Plotting the subtracted spectra with ggplot
```{r}
## Extract metadata, create a spectra data frame, merge the dataframes, and plot
# Extract sample names from spectra object
sample_names <- SFT_POM_MAOM[["names"]]

# Create a metadata data frame by parsing the sample names
metadata <- data.frame(
  Sample_Name = sample_names,
  Sample_Number = as.numeric(str_extract(sample_names, "^\\d+")),
  Sample_Type = str_extract(sample_names, "(POM|MAM)"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Assign Field_Location based on Sample_Number
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    Field_Location = case_when(
      Sample_Number >= 1 & Sample_Number <= 8  ~ "KB92",
      Sample_Number >= 9 & Sample_Number <= 16 ~ "KB31",
      Sample_Number >= 17 & Sample_Number <= 24 ~ "KB74",
      Sample_Number >= 25 & Sample_Number <= 32 ~ "KB95",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Treatment = ifelse((Sample_Number - 1) %% 8 < 4, "CN", "WC"),
    SOM_Fraction = ifelse(Sample_Type %in% c("POM", "PX"), "POM", "MAOM")
  )

# Create `spectra_df` with the wavenumber columns
wavenumbers <- SFT_POM_MAOM$freq
spectra_matrix <- SFT_POM_MAOM$data
sample_ids <- SFT_POM_MAOM$names

# Combine the wavenumber and spectral data into a data frame
spectra_df <- as.data.frame(spectra_matrix)
colnames(spectra_df) <- wavenumbers  # Set wavenumbers as column names
spectra_df <- cbind(Sample_ID = sample_ids, spectra_df)  # Add Sample_ID column

# Convert to long format for ggplot2
spectra_df_long <- spectra_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Sample_ID, names_to = "Wavenumber", values_to = "Intensity") %>%
  mutate(Wavenumber = as.numeric(Wavenumber))  # Ensure wavenumber is numeric

# Join with metadata
spectra_df_long <- left_join(spectra_df_long, metadata, by = c("Sample_ID" = "Sample_Name"))

# Plot only the untreated samples, color by treatment
sub_trt_plot <- ggplot(spectra_df_long, aes(x = Wavenumber, y = Intensity, color = Treatment, group = Sample_ID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 1, linewidth = 0.2) +  # Add alpha and size to make lines more distinct, no shading
  facet_wrap(~ Field_Location, scales = "free_y") +  # Facet by field
  scale_x_reverse() +  # Invert the x-axis
  scale_color_manual(values = c("CN" = "#1F77B4", "WC" = "#FF7F0E")) +
  labs(
    title = "POM & MAOM DRIFT Spectral Subtractions",
    x = "Wavenumber (cm⁻¹)",
    y = "Absorbance",
    color = "Treatment"
  ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
print(sub_trt_plot)

# To save
png("Sub_Spectra_Treatment_Facet_Field_KM.png", width=15, height=10, bg="white", res=600, units="in")
print(sub_trt_plot)
dev.off()

# Plot only the untreated samples, color by SOM fraction
sub_som_plot <- ggplot(spectra_df_long, aes(x = Wavenumber, y = Intensity, color = SOM_Fraction, group = Sample_ID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 1, linewidth = 0.2) +  # Add alpha and size to make lines more distinct, no shading
  facet_wrap(~ Field_Location, scales = "free_y") +  # Facet by field
  scale_x_reverse() +  # Invert the x-axis
  labs(
    title = "WOR & Control DRIFT Spectral Subtractions",
    x = "Wavenumber (cm⁻¹)",
    y = "Absorbance",
    color = "SOM Fraction"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

# Print the plot
print(sub_som_plot)

# Save the plot as a PNG file
png("Sub_Spectra_Fraction_Facet_Field_KM.png", width=15, height=10, bg="white", res=600, units="in")
print(sub_som_plot)
dev.off()
```

# Peak identification and resources

Margenot et al 2023 - https://doi.org/10.1002%2Fsaj2.20583

Singh et al 2016 (supplemental table) - 
https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/action/downloadSupplement?doi=10.2136%2Fsssaj2015.11.0414&file=saj2sssaj2015110414-sup-0001.pdf

Spectral assignments
3300 - 3400 OH and NH stretching ~ typical of cellulose, found in high OM soils, OH stretching in alcohols, carboxylic acids and phenols
2850 - 2950 Aliphatic C-H symmetric and asymmetric stretching
1730 - 1700 Esters and carboxylic acid
1650	      Aromatic C=C stretching vibration, Proteins
1635 - 1620 Aromatics and carboxyl C (1630)
1600 - 1621 Phenolic compounds and aromatic C=C (1610) or COO- stretching (1620)
1574 - 1575 Amide N-H bending vibration and amide stretching vibration C-N (amide II)
1525 - 1530 Aromatic stretching C=C
1500 - 1510 Aromatic C-H and C=C
1470	      Aliphatic bending vibration (C-H)
1400 - 1450 Aliphatics; CH2 (1400); aliphatic bending (1405); combination band due to bending and deformation and C-O (1432 - 1434); CH3 (1450)
1380 - 1390 Aliphatic bending vibration (C-H),potential contributions from carboxylate symmetric stretching vibration (C-O)
1360 	      CH2, CH3, and COO, COOH aliphatic bending
1348	      Aliphatics and phenolics
1320	      Hydroxyl C-O-H
1270	      Phenol C-O asymmetric stretching vibration, carboxylic acid stretching vibration (C-O)
1250	      Carboxylic COOH
1238	      Aromatic C-H in plane deformation
1000 - 1160 Polysaccharides, polysaccharide symmetric stretching vibration C-O (1080-1110)); carbohydrate C-OH stretching (1000-1030*)

```{r}
# Define peak wavenumbers observed
selected_peaks <- c(3300, 2931, 2871, 1724, 1660, 1600, 1575, 1540, 1510, 1470, 1405, 1360, 1320, 1275)

peak_labels <- c(
  "3300" = "3300 ν(OH, NH) stretch",
  "2931" = "2931 ν(C–H) asym. stretch (aliphatic CH2/CH3)",
  "2871" = "2871 ν(C–H) sym. stretch (aliphatic CH2/CH3)",
  "1724" = "1724 ν(C=O) stretch (carboxylic acids, esters)",
  "1660" = "1660 v(C=C) aromatic C=C stretching vibration",
  "1600" = "1600 v(C=C) phenolic and aromatic stretch",
  "1575" = "1575 ν(C-N, NH) stretch (peptides and amide)",
  "1540" = "1540 v(C=C) aromatic C=C stretch",
  "1510" = "1510 v(C-H) aromatic C-H and C=C",
  "1470" = "1470 δ(C-H) aliphatic bending",
  "1405" = "1405 δ(C-H) aliphatic bending",
  "1360" = "1360 δ(C-H) aliphatic bending",
  "1320" = "1320 v(O-H) C-O-H Hydroxyl",
  "1275" = "1275 ν(C=O) carboxylic acid COOH"
)
```

## Spectral Index Values
# Index 1 (Aliphatic : Aromatic) 2 (Aromatic : Carboxylic) and 3 (Aliphatic : Carboxylic)
In accordance with the wavenumber corresponding to the 13 organic bands described in Margenot et al 2015: https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.2136/sssaj2015.02.0070

# Margenot 2015 Indicies

Index 1 = (1650 + 920 + 840) / (2924 + 2850 + 1470 + 1405)

Index 2 = (2924 + 2850 + 1650 + 1470 + 1405 + 920 + 840) / (3400 + 1270 + 1110 + 1080)

# Helix 2026 Indices, Revised for Wood (aromatic hydrocarbon) Amendment

Index 1 = (2931 + 2871) / (1660 + 1600 + 1540 + 1510)

Index 2 = (1660 + 1600 + 1540 + 1510) / (1724 + 1320 + 1275)

Index 3 = (2931 + 2871) / (1724 + 1320 + 1275)

# First try Margenot et al., 2015 Indices, revised by SNT Santiago 2024
```{r}
# Note - the peak labels used here are as follows:
#peak_labels <- c(
#  "3300" = "3300 ν(OH, NH) stretch",
#  "2931" = "2931 ν(C–H) asym. stretch (aliphatic CH2/CH3)",
#  "2871" = "2871 ν(C–H) sym. stretch (aliphatic CH2/CH3)",
#  "1724" = "1724 ν(C=O) stretch (carboxylic acids, esters)",
#  "1660" = "1660 v(C=C) aromatic C=C stretching vibration",
#  "1601" = "1600 v(C=C) phenolic and aromatic stretch",
#  "1576" = "1575 ν(C-N, NH) stretch (peptides and amide)",
#  "1540" = "1540 v(C=C) aromatic C=C stretch",
#  "1510" = "1510 v(C-H) aromatic C-H and C=C",
#  "1469" = "1470 δ(C-H) aliphatic bending",
#  "1406" = "1405 δ(C-H) aliphatic bending",
#  "1320" = "1320 v(O-H) C-O-H Hydroxyl",
#  "1275" = "1275 ν(C=O) carboxylic acid COOH",
#  "1238" = "1238 v(C-H) aromatic plane deformation"
#)

# Define the wavenumbers for Index I and II (wavenumbers from Margenot et al., 2015)
#index1_numerator_wavenumbers <- c(1650, 920, 840)
#index1_denominator_wavenumbers <- c(2924, 2850, 1470, 1405)
#index2_numerator_wavenumbers <- c(2924, 2850, 1650, 1470, 1405, 920, 840)
#index2_denominator_wavenumbers <- c(3400, 1270, 1110, 1080)

# Define Revised wavenumbers (Suzette's Index)
# Reference Dissertation, by SUZETTE NICOLE TURNER SANTIAGO
# Deepening Our Understanding of Nitrogen Mineralization in the Soils of California’s Central Valley via Field Trials and Mid-Infrared Spectroscopy
index1_numerator_wavenumbers <- c(1650, 1238)
index1_denominator_wavenumbers <- c(2924, 2850, 1470, 1405)
index2_numerator_wavenumbers <- c(2924, 2850, 1650, 1470, 1405)
index2_denominator_wavenumbers <- c(3400, 1270, 1110, 1080)

# Combine all unique wavenumbers into one vector
index_wavenumbers <- unique(c(
  index1_numerator_wavenumbers,
  index1_denominator_wavenumbers,
  index2_numerator_wavenumbers,
  index2_denominator_wavenumbers
))

# Summarize the intensity values for Index I and II
# Find closest matches to the desired wavenumbers within a small tolerance (e.g., 1 cm⁻¹)
tolerance <- 2  # Adjust tolerance as needed
filtered_spectra <- spectra_df_long %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(Closest_Wavenumber = index_wavenumbers[which.min(abs(Wavenumber - index_wavenumbers))]) %>%
  filter(abs(Wavenumber - Closest_Wavenumber) <= tolerance) %>%
  ungroup()

# Replace negative intensity values with 0
filtered_spectra <- filtered_spectra %>%
  mutate(Intensity = ifelse(Intensity < 0, 0, Intensity))

# View the updated dataframe
head(filtered_spectra)

# Calculate Revised and optimized Index 1 and Index 2 and Index 3
indices <- filtered_spectra %>%
  group_by(Sample_ID) %>%
  summarize(
    Index_I = sum(Intensity[Closest_Wavenumber %in% c(1650, 1238)]) /
              sum(Intensity[Closest_Wavenumber %in% c(2924, 2850, 1470, 1405)]),
    Index_II = sum(Intensity[Closest_Wavenumber %in% c(2924, 2850, 1650, 1470, 1405)]) /
               sum(Intensity[Closest_Wavenumber %in% c(3400, 1270, 1110, 1080)])
  )

# View the results
print(indices)
# Optional: Export to CSV for review
write.csv(indices, "Index_I_and_II_subtractions_KM_rev.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Ensure indices includes metadata
indices <- indices %>%
  left_join(metadata, by = c("Sample_ID" = "Sample_Name"))

# Filter out extreme outliers
indices_filtered <- indices %>%
  filter(Index_I <= 20, Index_II <= 20)

# Plot Index I (Decomposition)
index_I_plot <- ggplot(indices_filtered, aes(x = Field_Location, y = Index_I, color = Treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ SOM_Fraction) +
  labs(
    title = "Index I: Degree of Decomposition",
    x = "Field Location",
    y = "Index I (Decomposition)",
    color = "Treatment"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("CN" = "#1F77B4", "WC" = "#FF7F0E"),
    labels = c("CN" = "Control", "WC" = "WOR")
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )
print(index_I_plot)

# Save the plot as a PNG file
png("index_I_KM_rev.png", width=10, height=6, bg="white", res=600, units="in")
print(index_I_plot)
dev.off()

# Plot Index II (recalcitrance)
index_II_plot <- ggplot(indices_filtered, aes(x = Field_Location, y = Index_II, color = Treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ SOM_Fraction) +
  labs(
    title = "Index II: Degree of Recalcitrance",
    x = "Field Location",

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("CN" = "#1F77B4", "WC" = "#FF7F0E"),
    labels = c("CN" = "Control", "WC" = "WOR")
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 12)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),

    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )
print(index_II_plot)
```

# Helix's Revised + Optimized Index 1, 2, 3
Aliphatic:Aromatic Index =      2931 + 2871               # Aliphatics
                            1660 + 1600 + 1540 + 1510     # Aromatics
            
Aromatic:Carboxylic Index =     1660 + 1600 + 1540 + 1510 # Aromatics
                            1724 + 1320 + 1275            # Carboxylic + COH
                          
Aliphatic:Carboxylic Index =      2931 + 2871             # Aliphatics
                            1724 + 1320 + 1275            # Carboxylic + COH

```{r}
# Define Revised and optimized wavenumbers
index1_numerator_wavenumbers <- c(2931, 2871)
index1_denominator_wavenumbers <- c(1660, 1600, 1540, 1510)
index2_numerator_wavenumbers <- c(1660, 1600, 1540, 1510)
index2_denominator_wavenumbers <- c(1724, 1320, 1275)
index3_numerator_wavenumbers <- c(2931, 2871)
index3_denominator_wavenumbers <- c(1724, 1320, 1275)

# Combine all unique wavenumbers into one vector
index_wavenumbers <- unique(c(
  index1_numerator_wavenumbers,
  index1_denominator_wavenumbers,
  index2_numerator_wavenumbers,
  index2_denominator_wavenumbers,
  index3_numerator_wavenumbers,
  index3_denominator_wavenumbers
))

# Summarize the intensity values for Index 1,2, 3
tolerance <- 2
filtered_spectra <- spectra_df_long %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(Closest_Wavenumber = index_wavenumbers[which.min(abs(Wavenumber - index_wavenumbers))]) %>%
  filter(abs(Wavenumber - Closest_Wavenumber) <= tolerance) %>%
  ungroup()

# Replace negative intensity values with 0
filtered_spectra <- filtered_spectra %>%
  mutate(Intensity = ifelse(Intensity < 0, 0, Intensity))

head(filtered_spectra)

# Calculate Revised and optimized Index 1,2,3
indices <- filtered_spectra %>%
  group_by(Sample_ID) %>%
  summarize(
    Index_1 = sum(Intensity[Closest_Wavenumber %in% c(2931, 2871)]) /
              sum(Intensity[Closest_Wavenumber %in% c(1660, 1600, 1540, 1510)]),
    Index_2 = sum(Intensity[Closest_Wavenumber %in% c(1660, 1600, 1540, 1510)]) /
               sum(Intensity[Closest_Wavenumber %in% c(1724, 1320, 1275)]),
    Index_3 = sum(Intensity[Closest_Wavenumber %in% c(2931, 2871)]) /
               sum(Intensity[Closest_Wavenumber %in% c(1724, 1320, 1275)])
  )

print(indices)
write.csv(indices, "Helix_Index123_raw.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Ensure indices includes metadata
indices <- indices %>%
  left_join(metadata, by = c("Sample_ID" = "Sample_Name")) %>%
  mutate(
    Years_Since_WOR = case_when(
      Field_Location == "KB95" ~ 3,
      Field_Location == "KB92" ~ 4,
      Field_Location == "KB74" ~ 6,
      Field_Location == "KB31" ~ 15
    ),
    Years_Since_WOR = factor(Years_Since_WOR, levels = c(3, 4, 6, 15))
  )

# Filter out extreme outliers
indices_filtered <- indices %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(Index_1), is.finite(Index_2), is.finite(Index_3),
    Index_1 <= 20, Index_2 <= 20, Index_3 <= 20
  )

write.csv(indices_filtered, "Helix_Index123_filt.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Plot Index 1
index_1_plot <- ggplot(indices_filtered, aes(x = Years_Since_WOR, y = Index_1, color = Treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ SOM_Fraction) +
  labs(
    title = "Aliphatic : Aromatic Index",
    x = "Years Since WOR",
    y = "Aliphatic : Aromatic Index Value",
    color = "Treatment"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("CN" = "#1F77B4", "WC" = "#FF7F0E"),
    labels = c("CN" = "Control", "WC" = "WOR")
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.1)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )
print(index_1_plot)

png("Ali.Aro_Index_KM_rev4.png", width=10, height=6, bg="white", res=600, units="in")
print(index_1_plot)
dev.off()
```
